name: The Hibbard household at 1701 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_hibbard_mrs_william_gold

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 1701 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 1701 Mrs. William Gold Hibbard; Frank Hibbard; Mrs. O. Van Schaack Ward.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 1701, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. The 1900 census (ED 40, T623 roll 245) was read for this card. The two live-in staff it lists at the house on 1 June 1900 are on the card, graded inferred because the count was taken four years before the scene. Left off: W. G. Hibbard (William Gold Hibbard died in 1903; the 1900 line names him with every other column blank). The children the Blue Book lists at the number from 1890 to 1911 are on the card with the years each was listed, whether or not they were at home in 1904. The 1910 census was not read for this card. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Lilian B. Hibbard
persons.note: Listed at 1701 under Mr. and Mrs. William G. Hibbard in the 1890 edition, and not after. That she was a daughter of the house is read from the shared surname and 'Miss' at the number; the Blue Book does not print the relationship.

persons.name: F. V. S. Hibbard
persons.note: Listed at 1701 under his parents in the 1894, 1895 and 1897 editions; in 1904 he and his wife keep their own house at 1620, on their own card. That they were a son of the house is read from the shared surname at the number; the Blue Book does not print the relationship. The Frank Hibbard listed at 1701 again from the 1905 edition is very likely the same man, but the book does not say so.

persons.name: William G. Hibbard jr.
persons.note: Listed at 1701 under his parents from 1894 to 1899, as William G. Hibbard jr.: the 'jr.' names him the son of the house. From the 1901 edition he and his wife are across the street at 1637, where they live in 1904 on their own card.

persons.name: Mrs. O. Van Schaack Ward
persons.note: Listed at 1701 in both editions. The Blue Book does not say how she was related to Mrs. Hibbard.

persons.name: Frank Hibbard
persons.note: First listed at 1701 in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904); the 1904 edition does not list him, so whether he was already here on 1 July 1904 is not documented. His relation to Mrs. Hibbard is not printed.

persons.name: Daniel Bain

born.note: The census gives March 1880, age 20 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Groom" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the rear building behind the house, as the head of his own household there (groom); born March 1880 (the figures are hard to read), in Scotland, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904. Part of the name is hard to read on the sheet; this is the best reading.

persons.name: James Halligan

born.note: The census gives November 1875, age 24 on 1 June 1900.

occupation.note: Written as "Horseman" in the occupation column on 1 June 1900.

persons.note: Enumerated on 1 June 1900 in the rear building behind the house, as a servant (horseman); born November 1875 (the figures are hard to read), in England, came to the United States in 1898, single. Servants changed places often, so this records who worked here in 1900; no source read says whether this person was still here on 1 July 1904.
